name: Puffing Billy Railway
note: Heritage steam railway (ride) between Belgrave, Emerald, Lakeside and Gembrook; the most popular Dandenongs attraction, and the ride is the draw with stops at named places.

name: Kokoda Memorial Track
note: Walking track: steep 1000-step staircase with historical plaques, Upper Ferntree Gully.

name: William Ricketts Sanctuary
note: Sculpture garden and bush sanctuary of the artist William Ricketts on Mount Dandenong Tourist Road.

name: Mount Dandenong
note: Summit lookout (633 m) with a view across Melbourne; the highest point of the Dandenong Ranges.

name: National Rhododendron Gardens
note: Public gardens of rhododendrons and azaleas in Olinda, open daily.

name: Cloudehill Gardens
note: Garden with themed garden rooms at Olinda, internationally known for its flowers.

name: Emerald Lake Park
note: Parkland around Lake Treganowan with walking trails, paddleboats and the Puffing Billy Lakeside visitor centre.

name: Eastern Dandenong Ranges Trail
note: Walking and cycling trail (17 km) alongside the Puffing Billy line from Clematis to Gembrook.

name: Dandenong Ranges National Park
note: National park covering four chunks of the Dandenong Ranges, with picnic grounds and walking tracks.

name: Ferntree Gully National Park
note: National park reached from Upper Ferntree Gully station, with walking tracks and picnic grounds.

name: Sherbrooke Forest
note: Forest reserve on the Dandenong Ranges' southern slopes, Sherbrooke and Belgrave; named as a Melbourne-area bushland but no visitor source names a specific visit here.

name: Olinda
note: Village (town) on the Mount Dandenong Tourist Road with gardens, tea rooms and views; a base for the Dandenong gardens.

name: Sassafras
note: Village in the Dandenong Ranges, named by Wikivoyage as a beautiful town in the forest.

name: Kallista
note: Village in the Dandenong foothills with heritage houses and gardens and a country atmosphere.

name: Belgrave
note: Town at the terminus of the Belgrave train line and the start of Puffing Billy, a gateway to the Dandenongs.

name: Gembrook
note: Small town at the eastern end of the Puffing Billy line and the Eastern Dandenong Ranges Trail.

name: Lysterfield Lake Park
note: Regional park around Lysterfield Lake with walking, cycling and picnic areas on the eastern edge of Melbourne.

name: Nobelius Heritage Park
note: Heritage park with the Emerald Museum, Emerald, of the Nobelius nursery and early horticulture.

name: Emerald Museum
note: Museum in Nobelius Heritage Park, Emerald, showing cultural material from the Dandenongs' early operations.

name: Running Rabbit Military Museum
note: Accredited military museum at Emerald, a small heritage display of Australian military history.

name: Yarra Ranges Regional Museum
note: Regional museum in the Yarra Ranges with exhibitions in a new architecturally designed building.

name: Upper Yarra Museum
note: Local history museum in the old railway station at Yarra Junction.

name: Montsalvat
note: Artists' colony in Eltham with galleries, a hall and a restaurant, open to visitors and dating to 1930s.

name: Ada Tree
note: Giant mountain ash estimated over 300 years old in the Yarra State Forest, reached by a short walk.

name: Gulf Station Historic Farm
note: Restored 19th-century working farm near Yarra Glen, where visitors see how a family lived on the land.

name: Mont De Lancey Historic Homestead
note: Historic homestead and cafe in the Yarra Valley, open to visitors from Melbourne.

name: Ngurrak Barring Art Trail
note: Public art trail linking Dandenong Ranges villages with art installations and sculptures on the mountain paths.

name: Silvan Dam Lookout
note: Lookout over Silvan Reservoir in the Dandenong Ranges, reached by a walking track.

name: Mount Dandenong Arboretum
note: Arboretum on the Mount Dandenong Tourist Road with a focus on southern hemisphere conifers.

name: Sugarloaf Reservoir
note: Reservoir near Yarra Glen where visitors picnic and barbecue at the reserve.

name: Yarra Glen Sunday Market
note: Sunday market at Yarra Glen; runs one day a week.

name: Healesville Car Boot Market
note: Car boot market behind Healesville's main street on the first Sunday of each month.

name: St Andrews Market
note: Saturday market at St Andrews in the Nillumbik hills; runs weekends only.

name: Yea
note: Small town on the Yea River at the northern edge of the region, a base for trails near Yea.

name: Healesville
note: Town at the eastern end of the Yarra Valley with the sanctuary, galleries, cafes and the Lilydale rail trail.

name: Healesville Sanctuary
note: Wildlife sanctuary run by Zoos Victoria with native animals and a breeding program, 4 km south of Healesville.

name: TarraWarra Museum of Art
note: Art museum with early Australian modernist paintings and contemporary exhibitions, overlooking the vineyards.

name: Yarra Valley Railway
note: Tourist railway operating from Healesville on weekends and public holidays.

name: Healesville Glass Blowing Studio
note: Glass studio where visitors can watch glass blowers at work and buy finished pieces.

name: Four Pillars Gin Distillery
note: Gin distillery in Healesville with tastings and tours, a venue for visitors rather than a landscape stop.

name: Maroondah Reservoir Park
note: Reservoir park about 5 km east of Healesville along the Maroondah Highway, with a picnic area and a walk.

name: Badger Weir
note: Weir and walking area near Healesville with a forest walk to Coranderrk and the Slip tracks.

name: Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail
note: Rail trail (40 km) for walking and cycling from Lilydale through the Yarra Valley to Warburton.

name: Lilydale
note: Town at the western gateway to the Yarra Valley and start of the Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail.

name: Yarra Glen
note: Town in the heart of the Yarra Valley wine district, with cafes and a Sunday market.

name: Coldstream
note: Small town on the Maroondah Highway in the Yarra Valley, with wineries and cafes nearby.

name: Warburton
note: Town in the Upper Yarra Valley and gateway to Mount Donna Buang, the rail trail and rainforest walks.

name: Yarra Junction
note: Small Upper Yarra town with the Upper Yarra Museum and access to the Warburton rail trail.

name: Kinglake
note: Town on the Kinglake ranges north of Melbourne, gateway to Kinglake National Park and the walk-up trails.

name: Hurstbridge
note: Town at the end of the Hurstbridge train line, with a large park and walking trails and the Wattle Festival (a seasonal event).

name: Marysville
note: Mountain town in the Yarra Ranges' eastern edge, base for Lady Talbot Drive, Steavenson Falls and Lake Mountain.

name: Domaine Chandon
note: Sparkling winery at Coldstream, with tastings and a restaurant; a winery venue visitors go to for tasting.

name: Yering Station
note: Historic winery and cellar door at Yarra Glen, one of the oldest vineyards in the Yarra Valley.

name: Helen's Hill Estate
note: Family winery cellar door with a restaurant overlooking the Yarra Valley entrance.

name: Oakridge Wines
note: Winery and restaurant on the Maroondah Highway at Coldstream, with views across the estate.

name: Tokar Estate
note: Spanish-inspired winery complex with a restaurant on the Maroondah Highway, Coldstream.

name: Hubert Estate
note: Winery, restaurant and art gallery with an event space, reopened in 2022 at Yarra Glen.

name: Whispering Hills
note: Small winery cellar door and coffee shop on the Warburton side of the valley.

name: Coombe Yarra Valley Melba's Garden Walk
note: Seven acres of century-old gardens with walks at Coombe Yarra Valley near Dixons Creek, a garden visitors walk through.

name: Edible Forest Yarra Valley
note: Edible plant forest within the Yarra Valley Estate property, a walk-through garden visitors can explore.

name: Alfred Nicholas Memorial Gardens
note: Historic gardens of the Burnham Beeches estate with extensive water features, Olinda area.

name: Rayner's Orchard
note: 40-acre working farm and orchard in the Yarra Valley with farm-gate produce and a shop.

name: CherryHill Orchards
note: Cherry-picking orchard in the Yarra Valley; picking is a summer-only activity at a permanent orchard.

name: Tesselaar KaBloom Festival of Flowers
note: Tulip and flower festival at Tesselaar's Dandenong Ranges flower farm; a seasonal festival, not a permanent spot.

name: Kuranga Native Nursery and Paperbark Cafe
wiki: Kuranga Native Nursery and Paperbark Cafe
note: Native plant nursery and cafe in the Dandenong foothills; a nursery visitors shop at.

name: Gilwell Park Adventure Centre
note: Scout adventure centre in bushland near Gilwell, used by groups; not a general visitor attraction.

name: Global Ballooning Australia
note: Hot-air balloon operator flying over Melbourne and the Yarra Valley; an operator, not a place.

name: Go Wild Ballooning
note: Hot-air balloon operator in the Yarra Valley; an operator, not a place.

name: Warburton Adventure Company
note: Adventure tour operator in Warburton offering guided hidden trails; an operator, not a place.

name: Yarra Valley X
note: Tour company based in Healesville; an operator, not a place.

name: Trees Adventure Glen Harrow Park
note: Tree-top ropes and zipline course in Belgrave; an operator run in a park.

name: Yarra Ranges National Park
note: National park covering the Upper Yarra and Warburton forests, Black Spur and Mount Donna Buang.

name: Black Spur
note: Scenic drive through the Black Spur ash forest in Yarra Ranges National Park between Healesville and Narbethong.

name: Mount Donna Buang
note: Mountain with a 21-metre lookout tower at 1,245 m, with views of the Dandenongs and Cathedral Range.

name: Donna Buang Rainforest Gallery and Skywalk
note: Boardwalk loop through cool temperate rainforest near Warburton, with a skywalk 15 m above the ground.

name: Big Culvert
note: Heritage-listed culvert on the Yarra Track at Cambarville; a short stop beside the road.

name: Cora Lynn Falls
note: Small secluded waterfall near Cambarville on the Marysville-Woods Point road.

name: Keppel Falls
note: Long cascade waterfall in the Taggerty River headwaters, reached by a walk from Lady Talbot Drive.

name: Steavenson Falls
note: One of Victoria's tallest waterfalls, reached by the Tree Fern Gully trail from Marysville.

name: Beeches Rainforest Walk
note: Short walk through cool temperate rainforest on Lady Talbot Drive, Marysville.

name: Lady Talbot Drive
note: Scenic drive from Marysville through waterfalls, walks and forest; a drive whose stops are its falls and walks.

name: Lake Mountain
note: Mountain resort above Marysville with cross-country skiing in winter and summit walks in summer.

name: Lake Mountain Summit Walk
note: Easy 4 km return walk from Lake Mountain with views of the Victorian Alps and Melbourne.

name: Kinglake National Park
note: National park on the slopes of the Great Dividing Range near Kinglake, with waterfall walks and the Andrew Hill summit.

name: Masons Falls
note: Waterfall in Kinglake National Park reached by a 700 m walk from Masons Falls Picnic Area.

name: Wombelano Falls
note: Hidden waterfall just north of Kinglake, a short easy walk.

name: Lyrebird Circuit Walk
note: 500 m accessible walk in Kinglake National Park past some of the park's oldest trees.

name: Running Creek Walk
note: 7.8 km walk through gullies and bush from the waterfall lookout in Kinglake National Park.

name: Andrew Hill Circuit
note: Circuit walk over the forested summit of Andrew Hill in Kinglake National Park.

name: Shepherds Track
note: Mountain-bike track near Kinglake, suitable only for downhill and enduro bikes.

name: Bollygum Park
note: Local adventure park with play equipment and a skate park in Kinglake, with a monthly sellers' market.

name: Cathedral Range State Park
note: State park with jagged ridges and hiking, reached from Lake Eildon's south-east side.

name: South Jawbone Peak
note: Summit reached by a 3.5 km return hike from the Jawbone car park in Cathedral Range State Park.

name: Lake Eildon National Park
note: National park around Lake Eildon's shore, with boating, camping and walking; on the Yea/Eildon edge.

name: Mount Cannibal Flora and Fauna Reserve
note: Flora and fauna reserve with native orchids and tree goannas near Yea.

name: Seven Acre Rock
note: Large rocky outcrop with views over Yarra State Forest and Bunyip State Park.

name: Peninsula Tunnels
note: Historic 19th-century gold-mining river diversion tunnels on the Yarra River, 14 km east of Warburton.

name: Backstairs Track
note: Walking track through a goldfields site and Mt Little Joe loop in the Upper Yarra region.

name: Big Pats Creek to Starlings Gap
wiki: Big Pats Creek to Starlings Gap
note: 9.6 km return hike through Yarra State Forest on a grade three track.

name: Morleys Track Dom Dom Saddle
note: 9.3 km one-way mountain-ash walk from Dom Dom Saddle to Fernshaw.

name: Dom Dom to Mount Donna Buang Walk
wiki: Dom Dom to Mount Donna Buang Walk
note: Hike across Mt Boobyalla, The Knobs and Mt Vinegar to Donna Buang; needs a car at each end.

name: Mount Victoria to Mount Donna Buang Walk
wiki: Mount Victoria to Mount Donna Buang Walk
note: Walk through mixed forest and mountain ash to Mount Donna Buang's lookout tower.

name: Warburton River Walk
note: Gentle 5 km walk beside the Yarra River in Warburton.

name: Wirrawilla Rainforest Walk
note: Easy circuit walk through temperate rainforest in Toolangi State Forest.

name: Toolangi State Park
note: State forest with a Discovery Centre and scenic trails near Toolangi, north of Healesville.

name: O'Shannassy Aqueduct Trail
note: 30 km walking and cycling trail along the historic aqueduct above the Upper Yarra Valley.

name: Reids Tramline Walk
note: Walk along relics of a historic horse and steam tramline in the forests of the Upper Yarra.

name: Richards Tramline Walk
note: 11 km walk past old tramline relics through forest near Marysville.

name: Australian Bicentennial National Trail
note: 5,330 km multi-use trail; the Healesville to Narbethong section passes through the region.

name: Tree Fern Gully Trail
note: Walk from Marysville to Steavenson Falls through tree fern gully.

name: Beauty Spot Walk Marysville
note: Short Marysville walk through flora and fauna, one of the town's most popular short walks.

name: Lilydale Airfield Scenic Flights
note: Light-plane sightseeing and flight training operator at Lilydale; an operator, not a place.

name: Lysterfield Lake
note: Lake in Lysterfield Lake Park with walking, a picnic area and a lakeside trail.

name: Art and Alchemy Gallery and Studio
wiki: Art and Alchemy Gallery and Studio
note: Gallery and studio in the Dandenong Ranges by the Silvan Dam Lookout; a working artist's gallery.

name: Tall Trees Studio
note: Working studio of a goldsmith on Mount Dandenong; a studio, not a visitor attraction.

name: Burrinja Cultural Centre
note: Arts and performance centre in Upwey with exhibitions and events, a venue rather than a landscape stop.

name: Silver Creek Walks Yea Road
note: Walking trails from Yea Road near Yea, on the Yea/Eildon edge of the region.
